chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said:

My father (peace be upon him), whenever he exited from his house, would say: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. I go out with the Might of Allah and His Strength, not by my might and my strength, but with Your Might and Your Strength. O Lord! I expose myself to Your sustenance, therefore bring it to me in well-being.'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for leaving the house in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication highlights the Imam's practice of explicitly renouncing personal agency ('la bi-hawlin minni') to affirm total dependence on God's power for sustenance. It serves as a practical model for integrating spiritual mindfulness into daily routines, linking physical departure with a request for health and provision.
